<!-- pr-reviewer: fd5767af0704c810dc43ebd669e323d6f37024b0 -->
Needs changes before merge. This is a SAFETY-tier review.

The review used current upstream laws at `61a817bed26bf42bf285638d5db337980bea6d0b`. The trial merge was clean. All builds and tests ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2893`. No GitHub runner ran.

### What looks good

- The cycle carries an explicit shift. The commands refuse a zero shift.
- The post engine refuses unsupported posts by name.
- The new app tests cover commands, undo, project files, MCP and posting.
- I read all 30 lines of `crates/post/tests/golden/fine_bore/haas.nc`. No existing NC or CL golden changed.
- The [Haas G76 reference](https://legacy-aem.haascnc.com/content/haascnc/en/service/codes-settings.type%3Dgcode.machine%3Dmill.value%3DG76.html) confirms the I/J shift form without Q. The [Haas G04 reference](https://www.haascnc.com/service/codes-settings.type%3Dgcode.machine%3Dmill.value%3DG04.html) explains integer P values in milliseconds.

### Results merged with main

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. The CL change selected batch coverage: 987 steps, zero failed, 39.3 minutes.
- The gate built the selected test targets and ran clippy with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- App `fine_bore_cycle`: 9 passed.
- UI library: 1292 passed, 7 ignored, zero failed. The suite ran from `crates/ui`.
- After all temporary probes were removed, motion `drilling::tests_fine_bore`: 6 passed. Sim `verify::fine_bore`: 4 passed.
- Heavy lanes: NOT RUN. The dry plan selects kernel, motion and app, with 249 steps. A dry plan is not a pass.

### Extra suites run

The changed golden directory is `crates/post/tests/golden/fine_bore/`. A source search found one reader: `crates/post/tests/fine_bore_cycle.rs`.

- `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-post --test fine_bore_cycle`: 8 passed in an explicit extra run.
- No importer code or STEP fixture changed. The importer-specific extra rule does not apply.

### Mutations rerun by the reviewer

Each baseline passed. Each mutation caused an assertion failure. Each restored test passed.

| Guard removed | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Motion `s >= room` refusal | `a_shift_the_bar_has_no_room_for_is_refused_by_name` | green / red / green |
| Sim `s < room` acquittal limit | `a_shift_with_no_room_for_the_bar_keeps_every_conviction` | green / red / green |

All temporary source edits were restored. No review evidence was committed.

### Requested before merge

1. **Keep solid-law holder collisions.** `crates/sim/src/verify/engine.rs:84` calls the acquittal after `section::solid`. The filter at `crates/sim/src/verify/fine_bore.rs:42` removes every `RapidInStock` warning at the stopped moves. This includes holder collisions from `solid.rs:220`. The band-reach law skips rapid moves. I reused the new holder fixture: tool radius 10, bar radius 8, holder radius 22, and shift X 0.5. The block extends from `(22.3, -5, 30)` to `(30, 5, 40)`. The solid law reports collisions, but the public verifier reports none:

   ```text
   solid alone: [RapidInStock { at: 2 }, RapidInStock { at: 3 }, RapidInStock { at: 4 }]; full verifier: []
   holder collision was removed: []
   ```

   Apply the acquittal only to warnings from law (d). Preserve the solid-law warnings. Add a test through the full verifier. The separate containment check in the drill app path does not correct this verifier result.

2. **Refuse a shift that rounds to zero in the output unit.** `assets/posts/haas.cps:944` checks the unformatted millimetre values. Line 971 then rounds I and J through `w`. With shift `(0.001, 0)` mm and `Units: "inch"`, the post reports no warning and writes:

   ```text
   G76 X0.3937 Y0.3937 Z-0.4724 R0.0787 I0. J0. P0 F2.36
   ```

   The posted cycle has no shift, so the tip can drag up the wall. Validate the output values before writing G76. Refuse an unrepresentable shift by name. Add an inch test for this case.

3. **Add before/after UI screenshots to the PR body.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs:273` adds the shift fields. The body has no screenshots. Put the images only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch and link them from the body.

4. **Run the reached heavy lanes on the final head.** `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:180` changes a safety path. The body states that no heavy lane ran. Current upstream `AGENTS.md:597` requires these results before readiness. Run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` after the fixes. Record the lanes and results in the body.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. The fine-bore acquittal now filters only law (d) warnings. It preserves solid-law holder collisions. Pin: `verify::fine_bore::tests::the_full_verifier_keeps_the_shifted_holder_collisions`.
2. The Haas post refuses a shift when both I and J round to zero in the output unit. It emits no G76. Pin: `haas_refuses_a_fine_bore_shift_that_rounds_to_zero_in_inch_output` in `camcraft-post` test binary `fine_bore_cycle`.
3. The PR body now links before and after UI screenshots. The images are only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `cc499a0ba118d918dcd4bc8672ac1e75d6eae61c`.
4. The final-head gates passed. Quick: 936 steps, zero failures. Gate clippy and explicit six-crate clippy passed. Heavy motion and app: 217 steps, zero failures. Supplemental kernel heavy: 13 steps, zero failures. Both `#1950` known-fail pins failed as expected.

Both new pins passed before mutation, failed with the fix removed, and passed after restore: GREEN / RED / GREEN.

New head: `c16ca2977db21332b6c810447ed083b74227d3dc`.

Please re-review this head.

Please fix ASAP.

This PR has the label `needs-rework`. The open items are in the latest review comment on this PR. Push a fix, or say that you keep this PR. The maintainer asked for this reminder.

<!-- pr-reviewer: c16ca2977db21332b6c810447ed083b74227d3dc -->
Clean SAFETY-tier review. No blocking finding. Ready for the maintainer to merge at the feature cut.

### Earlier findings

All four requests from the earlier review are met.

1. The acquittal filters only law (d). The public verifier keeps the solid-law holder collisions.
2. The Haas post checks the formatted shift. It refuses the inch case that would write zero I and J.
3. The body links before and after screenshots. I opened both images. They show the cycle and its shift fields. The images are on the fork's images branch.
4. The body records final-head heavy results. The author reports motion and app: 217 steps, zero failures. The supplemental kernel run has 13 steps, zero failures. Both known-fail pins failed as expected. I did not repeat these full heavy lanes.

### Results merged with main

All review builds and tests ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2893`. No GitHub runner ran.

The trial merge with upstream main `35d65e03be24407e9701cb6bafa5dedf79c6d72c` was clean. I used that main's AGENTS.md. Its text still matches the current upstream laws.

- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. 996 steps, zero failures, 31.9 minutes. Shared changes selected batch coverage.
- The gate built the test targets and ran clippy with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- Motion library: 493 passed, 11 ignored. Sim library: 204 passed.
- App `fine_bore_cycle`: 9 passed. Post `fine_bore_cycle`: 9 passed.
- UI library, from `crates/ui`: 1,335 passed, 7 ignored, zero failures.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16 cargo xtask gate light`: PASS. Release build and motion light twin: 2 steps, zero failures, 7.9 minutes.
- After the mutations were restored, sim `verify::fine_bore`: 5 passed. The focused post pin also passed.
- `git diff --check`: PASS. No temporary source edit remains.

### Extra suites run

The changed golden directory is `crates/post/tests/golden/fine_bore/`. A source search found one reader: `crates/post/tests/fine_bore_cycle.rs`.

- `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-post --test fine_bore_cycle`: 9 passed in an explicit extra run.
- No importer code or STEP fixture changed. The importer-specific extra rule does not apply.

### Mutations rerun by the reviewer

Each baseline passed. Each mutation failed at the expected assertion. Each restored test passed.

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Disable the Haas formatted-zero shift guard | `haas_refuses_a_fine_bore_shift_that_rounds_to_zero_in_inch_output` | green / red / green |
| Apply the acquittal to all warnings, after the solid law | `verify::fine_bore::tests::the_full_verifier_keeps_the_shifted_holder_collisions` | green / red / green |

The post mutation failed with `the unrepresentable shift is refused by name: []`. The verifier mutation failed with `holder collision at 2: []`.

### Golden and law checks

I read all 30 lines of the new `crates/post/tests/golden/fine_bore/haas.nc`. Both holes have the expected centre, bottom, R plane, I/J shift, dwell and feed. Each cycle is cancelled before the hop. No Q word is present. No existing NC or CL golden changed.

The [Haas G76 reference](https://legacy-aem.haascnc.com/content/haascnc/en/service/codes-settings.type%3Dgcode.machine%3Dmill.value%3DG76.html) confirms the I/J shift form when Q is absent.

The shift passes through undoable commands, the project file and MCP. Unsupported posts and a machine with orientation set to false refuse the cycle by name.

### Notes

No real control ran. Fine-bore-specific WCS transform tests remain absent, as the body states. Existing source files above 400 lines grew, including the project DTO files and the post engine. A later split can follow their domain seams.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Merge: the coordinator merges head c16ca2977. Review: mkinney's SAFETY-tier pr-reviewer marker on this head (clean; his clippy --all-targets -D warnings: PASS). Gate: stack-3 batch tier on the merged tree (local, Windows, 47af01c37). Every step that this PR owns is green: motion lib (493 passed, drilling tests_fine_bore included), post fine_bore_cycle (9), app fine_bore_cycle (9), ui lib (1338 passed, cycle_combo and holes_fine_bore included). The clippy step of that run stopped on a finding of a different PR (#3026), so it did not check crates/ui on the merged tree.
